newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinian Airlines takes to the skies.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Airlines takes to the skies.

text.p: Palestinian Airlines spread its wings on Wednesday, flying an inaugural scheduled commercial international flight from El-Arish airport in Egypt to Amman.
After a three-hour delay blamed on Israeli security measures, the small twin-propeller Fokker plane landed at Amman's Queen Alia airport to a festive welcome and offerings of celebratory cake.
Officials said they hoped the airlines would soon be flying from its home soil in the Gaza Strip rather than its temporary base in Egypt.

"We are landing at Queen Alia airport in the first flight of the Palestinian Airlines. We hope this flight will herald soon the start of flights from Gaza airport," Fayez Zaidan, head of the Palestinian Civil Aviation Authority, said on arrival.
Zaidan told reporters Israeli security measures delayed the plane's takeoff on the first of its planned twice-weekly trips between Jordan and El-Arish on Sundays and Wednesdays.
"The flight's takeoff was delayed for over three hours unfortunately because of the complicated Israeli measures on the land border post," he said.
The airline cannot fly from Palestinian-ruled Gaza until an airport is completed there and Israel gives approval for flights, but it has been operating charter flights from nearby El-Arish.
Palestinians wanted to start using Gaza airport to avoid the hassles which passengers are now encountering at the Israeli-controlled border, Zaidan added.
Captain Imad Qablawi, who flew the Fokker plane, said he was jubilant at having achieved a long-cherished dream to fly his national airlines plane.
"As a Palestinian pilot I have waited for this trip for a long time and have worked in many Arab airlines but when the Palestinian Airlines was set up I enlisted to join," he said.
Jordan's Civil Aviation Authority head Jasser Ziyad said the kingdom was looking forward to the day when the scheduled flights would be launched from Palestinian soil to boost ties.
Jordan was the first Arab country to give Palestinians permission to fly commercial flights to its airports, part of its efforts to support Palestinian statehood, Zayad said.
